import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Magic Squares

*References:*

* [Magic Square of Squares - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_square_of_squares)
* [multimagie.com](http://www.multimagie.com/English/SquaresOfSquaresSearch.htm)
* [Semi-Magic Square of Cubes](https://unsolvedproblems.org/index_files/SquareofCubes.htm)
* [Magic Square of Squares](https://static.nsta.org/pdfs/QuantumV6N3.pdf)
-/

namespace MagicSquares

/--
Does there exist a $3 \times 3$ matrix such that every entry is a distinct square,
and all rows, columns, and diagonals add up to the same value?

0 is excluded, as a Magic Square of Squares with 0 and 8 distinct squares is know is knownn.
See [Magic Square of Squares](https://static.nsta.org/pdfs/QuantumV6N3.pdf)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem exists_magic_square_squares :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ m : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℕ, ∃ t : ℕ,
       m.Injective2 ∧
       (∀ i j, 0 < (m i j) ∧ IsSquare (m i j)) ∧
       (∀ i, ∑ j, m i j = t) ∧
       (∀ j, ∑ i, m i j = t) ∧
       m 0 0 + m 1 1 + m 2 2 = t ∧
       m 0 2 + m 1 1 + m 2 0 = t := by
  sorry

/--
Does there exist a $3 \times 3$ semi-magic square whose entries are all distinct positive
integer cubes? A square is semi-magic if all rows and columns sum to the same total.

More precisely, we seek a $3 \times 3$ matrix with entries $a_{ij}$ such that each
$a_{ij} = n_{ij}^3$ for some positive integer $n_{ij}$, all nine cubes are distinct,
and all row sums and column sums are equal.

*Reference:*
[Semi-Magic Square of Cubes](https://unsolvedproblems.org/index_files/SquareofCubes.htm)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem exists_semi_magic_square_cubes :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ m : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℕ, ∃ t : ℕ,
       m.Injective2 ∧
       (∀ i j, ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ m i j = n ^ 3) ∧
       (∀ i, ∑ j, m i j = t) ∧
       (∀ j, ∑ i, m i j = t) := by
  sorry

end MagicSquares

findings.description: The docstring incorrectly says that a fully magic 3×3 square containing zero and eight other distinct squares is known. The cited January 1996 article did make this assertion, but Gardner subsequently corrected it: those examples are only semi-magic. This is a mathematical error in the explanatory prose, not in the Lean statement; positivity is actually redundant under the other conditions.
findings.source_evidence: Gardner, “The latest magic,” Quantum 6(4), March/April 1996, p. 60 (https://static.nsta.org/pdfs/QuantumV6N4.pdf): “In my article I said that order-3 squares made of squares are possible with zero in one cell. I should have added that squares of this type are magic only in rows and columns.” This corrects the assertion on p. 25 of the file’s cited https://static.nsta.org/pdfs/QuantumV6N3.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the assertion that a zero-containing fully magic square is known. If retaining an explanation, say that the known zero-containing examples are only semi-magic, citing Gardner’s correction, and that positivity does not change the fully magic existence question. No theorem-statement change is needed.

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly requires every square entry to be positive, whereas Wikipedia asks for nine distinct integer squares without explicitly excluding zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In any fully magic 3×3 square, the common sum is three times the center e, and each pair of opposite entries sums to 2e. For nonnegative entries, e = 0 would force all entries to vanish, contradicting distinctness. If any other entry were zero, its opposite would equal 2e, so both e and 2e would be nonzero integer squares, contradicting the irrationality of √2. Hence positivity follows from the remaining conditions. The exact existential statements with and without positivity were proved equivalent as positive_requirement_redundant in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorryAx.

review.notes: Both theorem statements faithfully express their source questions; no theorem-level misformalization or stale status was found. Injective2 enforces distinctness across all nine cells, both diagonals are correctly specified for the square problem, and the cube source explicitly requires distinct positive integer cubes and equal row/column sums only. Scratch files scratch.lean and boundaries.lean compile successfully. Checks cover zero and constant matrices, positivity of the common total, Sallows’s diagonal near-miss, and the cube source’s eight-cube near-miss.
